summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with xmlstarlet (a tool for parsing XML) pre-installed, sets up a demo directory containing sample XML data, customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji, and starts an interactive bash shell when the container runs.

explanations.3: This tells the installer not to prompt for user input during installation, which is necessary in Docker since there's no human to answer questions.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag tells the package manager to skip optional packages that aren't strictly required, keeping the container smaller.
explanations.8: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to reduce the image size since we won't need to install anything else later.
explanations.12: The printf command writes the XML content directly to a file; using printf instead of echo ensures we don't accidentally add a newline at the end.
explanations.18: This customizes the bash prompt so when you connect to the container, you see a whale emoji and other helpful information instead of the default prompt.
explanations.20: The -i flag tells bash to run in interactive mode, meaning it will accept commands you type in rather than just running a script and exiting.
